title: Improving Fairness in Graph Neural Networks via Mitigating Sensitive Attribute Leakage

problem.claim: Graph neural networks may inherit historical prejudices from training data and produce discriminatory predictions.

gap.claim: Existing fair GNN methods mostly borrow non-graph fair representation techniques without considering sensitive attribute leakage caused by feature propagation and changing feature correlations.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes Fair View Graph Neural Network, which identifies and masks features correlated with sensitive attributes while accounting for correlation variation after feature propagation.
The method adaptively clamps encoder weights to avoid using features related to sensitive attributes.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that feature propagation can change correlations between previously innocuous non-sensitive features and sensitive attributes.
Experiments on real-world datasets reportedly show that FairVGNN achieves a better trade-off between model utility and fairness.

narrative_sequence.summary: GNNs learn node representations on graphs but may inherit bias from training data.
Existing fair GNN approaches overlook sensitive attribute leakage and correlation changes caused by feature propagation.
The authors design correlation-based feature masking strategies and propose FairVGNN to generate fair feature views.
FairVGNN adaptively clamps encoder weights to avoid sensitive-related features.
Real-world dataset experiments report an improved utility–fairness trade-off.

source_observation.claim: Feature propagation can alter correlations between non-sensitive and sensitive features.

interpretation.claim: Fairness interventions for graph models should account for representation changes induced by propagation rather than relying only on pre-propagation correlations.

application.claim: Evaluate and mitigate sensitive-feature leakage after graph propagation when designing fair GNNs.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the approach generalizes beyond the reported real-world datasets or across all graph settings.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, baselines, metrics, or numerical results.
The abstract does not provide implementation details for the masking strategies or adaptive weight clamping.
The abstract does not establish causal effects or independent verification of the reported fairness–utility trade-off.
